Waihau Bay HallBoyWaihau Bay, 1984. Fried bread's on.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersFried bread with golden syrupPuffy fried bread squares served warm with butter and golden syrupHow to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast1 tbsp caster sugar1 tsp salt325ml warm water2 L vegetable oil, for frying60g butter, to serve125ml golden syrupMix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water into a soft dough and knead briefly.Prove the dough until doubled, which is the resting time.Roll out 2cm thick and cut into 12 squares.Heat the vegetable oil to 175°C and fry a few at a time until puffed and golden on both sides.Serve warm with butter and golden syrup.Rocky's special powers corn frittersCreamed corn and spring onion fritters fried crispHow to make it420g creamed corn200g corn kernels150g self-raising flour2 eggs3 spring onions100ml vegetable oil, for frying125ml sweet chilli sauceMix the creamed corn, kernels, flour, eggs and sliced spring onion.Fry heaped tablespoons in oil until golden on both sides, in batches.Drain and serve hot with sweet chilli sauce.Fish shop hot chips with garlic aioliThe fish and chip shop down the road from Waihau BayHow to make itAs written, serves 4Thick-cut chips fried twice until crunchy outside and fluffy inside, salted hot, wrapped in paper with a garlicky aioli and tomato sauce.Cut 1.2kg floury potatoes into 1.5cm chips, soak in cold water for 30 minutes and pat dry.Heat oil to 150°C and fry in batches for 6 minutes until soft but pale.Drain and rest 15 minutes.Heat the oil to 190°C and fry again for 3 minutes until golden and crunchy.Salt straight away.Mix 150g mayo with 2 crushed garlic cloves and a squeeze of lemon.Serve in paper with the aioli and tomato sauce.MainsShogun's homecoming hāngī-style porkPork shoulder, kūmara, pumpkin and potato roasted under cabbage in foilHow to make it1.2kg pork shoulder2 tsp salt600g kumara600g butternut pumpkin400g potatoes1 cabbage1 roll foil, to wrapSeason the pork well. Cut the kumara, pumpkin and potatoes into chunks.Line a deep roasting tin with cabbage leaves and add the pork and vegetables. Cover with more cabbage and wrap tightly in foil.Roast at 160°C until the pork falls apart.Rest and shred the pork, then serve with the vegetables.Nan's savoury mince on buttered toastWhat's in the pot at Nan's houseHow to make itAs written, serves 4Beef mince simmered with onion, carrot, peas and a rich gravy until thick, spooned over thick buttered toast with grated tasty cheese on top.Brown 600g beef mince in a large pan, breaking it up.Add 1 diced onion and 1 grated carrot and cook 5 minutes.Stir in 1 tbsp plain flour, 2 tbsp tomato sauce, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 400ml beef stock.Simmer 15 minutes until thick, adding 150g frozen peas for the last 5.Toast 8 thick slices of white bread and butter well.Spoon the mince over and top with 80g grated tasty cheese.SweetsHokey pokey ice creamVanilla ice cream folded through crunchy honeycomb toffeeHow to make it100g caster sugar2 tbsp golden syrup1 tsp bicarbonate of soda1 L vanilla ice cream, slightly softenedHeat the sugar and golden syrup until bubbling and golden.Take off the heat, whisk in the bicarbonate of soda and pour onto baking paper to set.Smash into small pieces and fold through the softened ice cream.Refreeze until firm.DrinksCrazy Horses dairy lime milkshakeMilk, vanilla ice cream and lime cordial blended frothyHow to make it600ml full cream milk, cold4 scoops of vanilla ice cream4 tbsp lime cordialBlend the milk, ice cream and lime cordial until frothy.Pour into 4 tall glasses and serve straight away with straws.Homebrew ginger beerShogun's orders.
